items.description: Account/device REST gateway per region group. Group USA -> gw-us, EU -> gw-eu, SEA (and others) -> gw-sg, China -> api.xiaoyi.com. HTTPS, host names are vendor constants.

The region group is chosen from the account's country code, NOT discovered from the server: assets/locale.json maps each country code to server USA|EU|SEA (245 entries: EU 111, SEA 81, USA 53). The app stores the picked country in 'LoginSelectedCountry'. A wrong country sends the login to the wrong gateway.

items.description: Password sign-in is GET {gateway}/v4/users/login with query params seq=1, account=<e-mail> (CHN build uses email= or mobile=), password=<hashed, see kami.auth.password_hash>, dev_name, dev_type, dev_os_version. No signature on this call. The password is therefore in the URL query (HTTPS only).

The password is never sent in clear: password = base64(HMAC-SHA256(key = a static app string constant, msg = password UTF-8)), no line wraps. The key is a Java string constant in the APK (vendor secret; value deliberately NOT recorded here). Needs the owner decision in the scout report before it may enter public source.

evidence.snippet: HmacSHA256 over the password; key = constant field f104281a (value not recorded)

items.description: Success is JSON {code:20000, data:{userid, token, token_secret, name, img, register_time, flag, aiOptionFlag, ...}}. token + token_secret are the session credentials used to sign later calls. The app keeps them in memory/prefs; no expiry time is returned or tracked client side.

Login result codes seen in the callback: 20000 ok; 20281 handed to a separate callback (extra step, meaning not proven); 20282 makes the app retry the third-party login with opt flag '1'; 30301 and -10003 are passed to the UI as distinct errors; anything else is a plain failure. Exact meanings need the strings/UI or a real response.

Every call after sign-in adds seq=1, userid=<userid> and hmac=base64(HMAC-SHA1(key = token + '&' + token_secret, msg = 'k1=v1&k2=v2...')). The message is the parameters in the map's iteration order (insertion order for LinkedHashMap, sorted for TreeMap callers) joined with & and NOT url-encoded; the hmac param itself is excluded. Key material comes from the login response, not from the APK.

items.description: Third-party sign-in (Google/Facebook/Apple style) uses POST/GET /v4/auth/login with form fields code, user_sub, user_name, type, token, reftoken, expires, opt_type, email, dev_*. If the owner's Kami account was created with a social login there may be no password at all; the account would need a password set in the app first.

Captcha-style validation code: GET /v4/users/validation_code returns an image/code id; POST /v4/users/validation_code with validationCodeId verifies. Registration (/v4/users/register) and password reset (request_reset_pwd) carry validationCodeId. The plain login call does NOT carry one.

No second factor is part of /v4/users/login in this build. The only code flows found are: e-mail code for security property edits (/v4/users/security_prop, request_edit_security_prop), SMS OTP for mobile (/v8/user/mobile/send/otp, verify/otp) and e-mail verify (/v4/users/email/verify_code). 20281/20282 may be a new-device or social-bind step (unproven).

GET/POST /v4/users/auth_token with userid, token, hmac, country and appName=kami is the token check used when the app restores a stored session. No refresh-token exchange for password accounts was found.
GET {gateway}/v5/devices/list?seq=1&userid=<id>&hmac=<signed>. Response data[] has one object per camera (owned and shared, see 'share'/'accessRight').

Per-device JSON fields read by the app: uid (also used as DID and P2P id), name, model, did, flag, share, category, count, type, interVersion, accessRight, state, online (bool), password (encrypted), relayFlag, groupBindable, webPairStatus, and ipcParam (a JSON string with p2p_encrypt, ssid, mac, ip, rssi, battery, wakeup, signal_quality).

Online state has two sources: (1) the list's 'online' boolean (cheap, REST); (2) for P2P cameras the app also asks over the P2P layer (PPPP_CheckDevOnline for TNP, getOnlineStatus command). The REST flag is enough for a camera list.

Each camera has its own P2P view password. Server field 'password' is AES-128-ECB/PKCS7 encrypted with key = first 16 chars of the UID; the plaintext is the camera password used for all P2P commands. If the field is empty the app uses the default '888888'. The account name is always 'admin'. No app-wide secret is involved (the key is the UID).

For TNP cameras: GET /v4/tnp/device_info (uid + signed) returns data.DID (a string like TNP-xxx-yyy that also fixes the transport type), data.InitString (the P2P server list for the native library) and data.License (per-device license key, 'x:y' where the second part is the device key). These three feed PPPP_Initialize/PPPP_Connect. Cached in prefs as TNP_DID_/TNP_SEV_/TNP_KEY_<uid>.

Transport per camera: P2PDevice.type 0 = TUTK (UID is upper/mixed case), 1 = Langtao (all-lowercase id), 2 = TNP (DID matching TNP-a-b), 3 = TX (declared, no factory branch). AntsCameraManage builds AntsCameraTutk / AntsCameraLangtao / AntsCameraTnp from it. Which model uses which cannot be read from the APK; it is server data per device.

Sharing is server side: /v5/deviceshare/{invite,accept,friends,shareddetail,record,invitee/invitations,invitor/invitations}. A shared camera appears in the same devices/list with share=true and an accessRight value.
Rename/edit uses /v2/devices/edit (userid, uid, name, message + signature).

items.description: Cloud-stored clips (paid Kami Cloud) are plain HTTPS: GET /vas/v8/cloud/videos (returns a map of URLs), /vas/v8/cloud/videos/quickview (per-day index), /vas/v8/cloud/ts/metadata (segment list), /vas/v8/cloud/images (thumbnails), /vas/v8/cloud/service (plan state), DELETE /vas/v8/cloud/videos. The app parses HLS playlists locally. Gated by a Cloud plan.
Motion/AI alert list: /v5/alert/events (and /v4/alert/events, /v5/alert/events/top), push settings /v5/alert/push_prop. Plain REST with the same signature.

libkami_core.so (the 'phone as camera' feature) talks to the same cloud with hmac-signed URLs (/v6/ipc/on_line, /v4/alert/event, /vas/v8/ipc/ball/STSToken). Not needed for a viewer client, listed so nobody mistakes it for the viewer path.

Live video does not use HTTPS/RTSP/WebRTC. Three vendor P2P stacks sit behind one AntsCamera class: TUTK (IOTC+AVAPI, libIOTCAPIs/libAVAPIs), TNP (YI's own 'PPPP'-based stack, libPPPP_API, Java wrapper com.tnp.TnpCamera) and Langtao (libglnkio, 32-bit only). Constants TYPE_TUTK=0, TYPE_LANGTAO=1, TYPE_TNP=2.

TUTK path: IOTC_Initialize2(0) (no license key passed from Java), IOTC_Get_SessionID, IOTC_Connect_ByUID_Parallel(uid, sid), then avClientStart2(sid, account, password, timeout...). When p2p_encrypt is true the account is a random 15-char nonce and the password is derived from it (see kami.media.command_auth). Needs the vendor's native TUTK stack.

evidence.snippet: iAvClientStart2 = AVAPIs.avClientStart2(TutkCamera.this.mSID, strGenNonce, password, avClientStartTimeOut, iArr, 0, this.resend);

items.description: TNP path: PPPP_Initialize(InitString bytes, 12) once, then PPPP_Connect(p2pid, flag, 0, serverString, licenseDeviceKey) (or PPPP_WakeUp_And_Connect for battery cameras), PPPP_Check(session) for NAT/relay info, then PPPP_Read/PPPP_Write on channels. NAT traversal, relay selection and the session crypto are inside libPPPP_API.so. serverString and licenseDeviceKey come from kami.cloud.tnp_device_info.

Above the PPPP byte pipe the TNP protocol is plain Java: an 8-byte TNPHead {version, ioType(1 video, 2 audio, 3 command), abilityRet, reserved, dataSize u32}; commands add a 40-byte TNPIOCtrlHead {commandType u16, commandNumber u16, exHeaderSize u16, dataSize u16, authInfo[32]}; video/audio use TNPFrameHead then a 24-byte AVFrame header. Byte order is a per-camera flag. This part is reimplementable once a PPPP session exists.

Per-command / per-session authentication (TNP and TUTK, when p2p_encrypt): nonce = random string from [A-Za-z0-9] (TNP: noncePrefix(7) + 8 chars; TUTK: 15 chars); user = nonce; pass = first 15 chars of base64(HMAC-SHA1(key = camera password, msg = 'user=xiaoyiuser&nonce=' + nonce)). Without p2p_encrypt, account 'admin' and the plain password are sent. The camera password comes from kami.cloud.camera_password. No app-wide secret.

Live view is started by an IOCTRL: IOTYPE_USER_IPCAM_START2 (8190) when p2p_encrypt else IOTYPE_USER_IPCAM_START (511), payload = a use-counter. Stop is IOTYPE_USER_IPCAM_STOP (767). Audio start 768, speaker (talk-back) start 848.

Media is not fully encrypted. When p2p_encrypt is true only the first two 16-byte blocks of each I-frame payload (offsets 4 and 20) are AES-128-ECB encrypted with key = camera password + '0'; P/B frames are clear. Audio frames are AES-ECB per 16-byte block. Key comes from the account's device list, so a client with the password can decrypt in pure Python.

Video H.264 (78) and H.265 (81), also MJPEG/MPEG4/H263 ids; audio AAC (138), ADPCM, PCM (140), Speex, MP3, G.726 (143). FFmpeg can decode all of them from an Annex-B/ADTS byte stream; the app also ships a separate libh265decoder.

A camera allows few concurrent P2P sessions. The TNP wrapper defines device-side errors ERROR_PPPP_DEVICE_KICK (-3100) and ERROR_PPPP_DEVICE_KICK_MAX_SESSION (-3101); PPPP_APIs also has ERROR_PPPP_DEVICE_MAX_SESSION (-3029). A PC client opening a stream can therefore push the phone's live view out (or be pushed out).

The TNP library enforces signed access: error codes include INVALID_APILICENSE (-3021), INVALID_SERVER_STRING (-3023), INVALID_SIGNATURE (-3034), INVALID_TICKET (-3032), INVALID_TIMESTAMP (-3033), INVALID_TOKEN (-3037). So a client without the per-device InitString/License (cloud) or without the native signing cannot connect. This is not the open 'CS2 PPPP' handshake documented by community projects.

evidence.snippet: Community notes on libPPPP_API (CS2-style UDP camera protocol); archived. Proves a related protocol exists, not that it matches Kami TNP.

items.description: Stock firmware has no RTSP/ONVIF. The only RTSP/ONVIF route is custom firmware (yi-hack family), which modifies the camera and is out of scope.

items.description: All camera controls and SD-card playback are IOCTRL command numbers (203 IOTYPE_USER_IPCAM_* constants) sent over the same P2P session, wrapped by CameraCommandHelper (250 KB) with request/response structs in AVIOCTRLDEFs. Pure Python is possible once a session exists; struct layouts are in Java.

SD playback: list events with IOTYPE_USER_IPCAM_LISTEVENT_REQ (792) / RESP (793), then IOTYPE_USER_IPCAM_RECORD_PLAYCONTROL (794; 12718 '2' variant when p2p_encrypt) with a play-record struct and time. Video then arrives on the normal frame channel.

Per-model capabilities (PTZ, alarm, h265, audio mode, cloud, ...) are shipped as assets/feature_config/config_<model>.json (61 files) plus a base file. A client can read them offline to decide which controls to show.

unresolved.detail: Decided by server data per device (UID/DID format), not by a model table in the APK. Needs the owner's model and one device-list reply.
Session setup, relay selection, signed tickets and channel crypto are inside libPPPP_API.so. Stopped here: needs native RE (own decision).
Java passes no license key to IOTC_Initialize2(0); where the license lives (native lib or device side) is unknown.
No constant named PTZ was found in AVIOCTRLDEFs; PTZ goes through another command id in CameraCommandHelper. Not traced.
Flutter module logic not inspected; if the account/device flow also lives there, the REST facts above still hold for the Java path.
